name: DME Limits — DMX.1
description: Resolve the PX_DMX hard edit: confirm the DMEMAXMET message, rule out procedure E1399, review the DMERNTMX accumulator and the NU modifier, obtain the DME purchase price ($5000) and the history allowance ($3000), reprice the claim to the correct $2000 allowance, deny the excess with EOB PX_00256, bypass PX_DMX with PX_DX, and Pay.

steps.name: Identify the PX_DMX hard edit
steps.description: The Event Resolution tab lists every edit on the claim. PX_DMX is the hard edit highlighted with an error indication — this is the current event to resolve. PX_DMY is also present, but it is a soft edit and needs no claim action, so nothing ranks above PX_DMX in the event hierarchy.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Event Resolution tab is opened.
steps.hint: PX_DMX is the only hard edit. PX_DMY is a soft edit — informational only.
steps.checklistItem: Event Resolution opened — PX_DMX hard edit identified, PX_DMY is a soft edit

steps.name: Confirm the DMEMAXMET message
steps.description: Open the Notes tab and confirm that the DMEMAXMET message is present in the WGS notes. DMEMAXMET is the system's signal that the member has already met the DME maximum for this provider and procedure. If the message is present, proceed. In this scenario it is present.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Notes tab is opened.
steps.hint: Look for the DMEMaxMet line in the WGS Notes section.
steps.checklistItem: DMEMAXMET message confirmed present in the WGS notes

steps.name: Check the procedure code is not E1399
steps.description: Validate whether the procedure code on the claim is E1399 by checking the Procedure code field on the Claim Lines tab. E1399 is a miscellaneous DME code that follows separate alternate guidelines. In this scenario the procedure code is E0562, so E1399 does not apply and the trainee proceeds. Note the modifier while you are here — NU means the DME was purchased, RR means it was rented.Here,the Modifier present under the claim lines tab is RR.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the Claim Lines tab is opened.
steps.hint: The procedure code is E0562 — not E1399 — so the alternate guidelines do not apply.
steps.checklistItem: Procedure code is E0562, not E1399 — main path applies

steps.name: Review the DME rental accumulator and modifier
steps.description: Navigate to Search → Benefits and open the Accumulators screen. Expand the OTHER group and look for DMERNTMX (DME RENTAL MAX PROV/PROC). It carries what the member has already accrued against the DME cap for this provider and procedure: a Visit row accrued 1, and a Dollars row accrued 3000. Combined with the NU modifier on the claim line (NU = purchased, RR = rented), this tells you the DME was bought and the purchase-price cap has already been partly consumed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the OTHER accumulator group is expanded — not on merely opening the Benefits sub-tab.
steps.hint: The accumulator is under OTHER — click it to expand and find DMERNTMX.
steps.checklistItem: DMERNTMX found under OTHER — Visit 1 / Dollars 3000 accrued; modifier NU = purchased

steps.name: Change the Pricing modifier from RR to NU
steps.description: In the Search tab itself,move to the Pricing sub-tab. In the Claim Lines section the Modifier input states as RR (rented). Because this DME was purchased, change it to NU. Pricing a purchased item as a rental would return the rental rate, not the purchase price.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the Pricing Modifier input is set to NU.
steps.hint: RR = rented, NU = purchased. This DME was purchased — type NU.
steps.checklistItem: Pricing modifier changed from RR to NU

steps.name: Obtain the DME purchase price
steps.description: Still in the Claim Lines section of the Pricing sub-tab, change the Billed amount to 100000 — only in this section, never on the claim itself. A billed amount far above any possible price stops the pricing engine from capping the result at what was charged, so what comes back is the true purchase price. Click Get Pricing: the purchase price appears in the Allowed column. In this scenario it is $5,000.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when Get Pricing is clicked AND the Billed amount equals 100000. Clicking with any other billed amount does not reveal the purchase price and does not complete the step.
steps.hint: Set the Billed amount to 100000, then click Get Pricing. The purchase price shows under Allowed.

steps.name: Review history for a prior DME allowance
steps.description: In the Search tab itself,go to the Claims sub-tab and review the member's claim history for this provider. Check whether the same DME was previously allowed and note the amount. Click Open claim detail on the history claim: its Claim Lines tab shows procedure code E0562 and its Summary shows an allowed amount of $3,000. So $3,000 of the purchase price has already been paid out.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the history claim detail pop-up is opened.
steps.hint: Click Open claim detail — read the procedure code on Claim Lines and the allowed amount on Summary.
steps.checklistItem: History claim reviewed — procedure E0562 previously allowed for $3,000

steps.name: Get pricing and calculate the correct allowance
steps.description: Return to the Pricing sub-tab, scroll down to Pricing Results, and click Get Pricing to obtain the allowed amount the system is suggesting for the current claim. In this scenario it suggests $4,000. But the claim may only pay up to the purchase price: take the amount already allowed on history for this procedure code and subtract it from the purchase price. $5,000 (purchase price) − $3,000 (history allowed) = $2,000. So the correct allowance is $2,000, not the $4,000 the system suggests.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when Get Pricing is clicked in the Pricing Results section.
steps.hint: The system says $4,000 — but $5,000 − $3,000 = $2,000 is the correct allowance.
steps.checklistItem: System allowance $4,000 obtained — correct allowance is $2,000

steps.name: Enter EOB code PX_00256
steps.description: Go to the Claim Lines tab. The claim may only pay up to the purchase price, so the amount over it must be denied. Enter EOB code PX_00256 (non-covered) in the EOB code box on the Repricing section.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the EOB code input is set to PX_00256.
steps.hint: EOB code PX_00256 is the non-covered code.
steps.checklistItem: EOB code PX_00256 entered on the claim line

steps.name: Enter the non-covered amount of $2,000
steps.description: Enter the non-covered amount in the Repricing section: $2,000 — the amount over the correct allowance that must be denied. After the claim is validated the line settles at Billed $5,000 / Allowed $2,000 / Write-off $1,000, replacing the system's Billed $5,000 / Allowed $4,000 / Write-off $1,000.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the Non-covered amount input is set to 2000.
steps.hint: Deny the amount over the purchase price — $2,000.

steps.name: Apply the PX_DX bypass code and validate
steps.description: Return to the Event Resolution tab to find the bypass code. Select the PX_DX bypass code and click the Validate button in the claim summary to bypass the PX_DMX event. On validation the claim line settles at Billed $5,000 / Allowed $2,000 / Write-off $3,000.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the trainee clicks the claim summary Validate button while the selected bypass code is PX_DX. Any other code shows an invalid-bypass status and does not complete the step.
steps.hint: In the Bypass Codes section pick 'PX_DX — Bypass the DME maximum edit', then click Validate in the claim summary bar.
steps.checklistItem: PX_DX bypass applied and validated — amounts settled to Allowed $2,000 / Write-off $3,000

steps.name: Submit the Pay decision
steps.description: The claim now pays only up to the purchase price. Go to the Decision section in the header, select 'Pay' from the dropdown, and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the decision submitted is Pay.
steps.hint: Select Pay in the header decision dropdown, then Submit.
